This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Lines gated on their own kernel feature need it named to run their unit tests.
# The K3 command also names the kernels crate, whose K3 tests ride the same
# feature:
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-k3 -p pegainfer-kernels --features k3 --lib
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-glm52 --features glm52 --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |

| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |

| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |

```bash
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. - `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt

- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). - `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52

              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │

                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

2	
3	## 1. 本讲目标
4	
5	本讲精读 `pegainfer-kv-offload/src/layout.rs`——整个 crate 里数学密度最高的 100 行。学完后你应该能够：
6	
7	1. 给定 `(num_layers, kv_heads, head_dim, page_size, num_blocks)`，**手算**出 `kv_block_len / layer_stride / page_stride`（元素数）与 `layer_bytes / page_stride_bytes`（字节数），进而写出每个 layer arena 的 `base_ptr` 偏移、`bytes_per_block`、`block_stride_bytes` 与整个 `Registration` 的 `size_bytes`。
8	2. 解释 `KvArena` 这个抽象如何用**同一套五个字段**统一两种截然不同的显存形态：qwen3 的融合（fused）布局与 GLM5.2 的 MLA latent + index-K sidecar 布局。
9	3. 推导 `size_bytes = (num_blocks − 1) × block_stride + bytes_per_block` 为什么是「最后一块的到达界」，而 `num_blocks × stride` 会谎报一段根本不属于本 arena 的尾巴。
10	
11	本讲不涉及任何 I/O——`layout.rs` 是纯几何，全部逻辑可以在脑子里、纸上跑通。这是它适合作为进阶层第二讲的原因：把地址算对，后面 save/load 的每一步才有意义。
12	
13	## 2. 前置知识
14	
15	承接 u1-l2（KV 卸载心智模型）与 u2-l1（配置层）。本讲需要以下几个概念，先用人话过一遍：
16	
17	- **块（block）与页（page）**：pegainfer 把 KV cache 按 `page_size`（通常 16）个 token 一组切成块。块是搬运单位——save 存的是块，load 恢复的也是块，块的内容寻址键（哈希链）在 u1-l2 讲过。
18	- **bf16**：brain float 16，2 字节浮点。KV cache 的每个元素是 bf16，所以 `std::mem::size_of::<half::bf16>() == 2`。`pegainfer-kv-cache` 的 `KvLayout` 里所有 stride 都以**元素数**计；要换算成字节必须 ×2。这是本讲最容易算错的一步。
19	- **stride（步长）与 size（大小）**：一段内存里「相邻两块起点之间的距离」叫 stride，「一块实际占多少字节」叫 copy size / bytes_per_block。GPU 拷贝原语（`cuMemcpyAsync`）只吃**连续区间**；当数据不连续时，就必须告诉底层「每次拷多少、下一块隔多远」——这两个数解耦，正是 `block_stride_bytes` 与 `bytes_per_block` 分开存在的原因。
20	- **融合（fused）布局**：所有层的 KV 挤在一整块显存分配里，页内按层交错（详见 4.2）。
21	- **sidecar（边车）布局**：主 KV 之外，每层还有独立分配的辅助状态（GLM5.2 的 index-K），与主 KV **共享同一个块号池**——块号 `b` 同时索引主 KV 的第 `b` 块和 sidecar 的第 `b` 块。
22	- **注册（registration）**：把 GPU 显存里「哪些区间属于哪些层、块怎么排布」告诉 pegaflow 的一次性动作。注册之后 save/load 都不再传地址，只传 `(层名, 块号)`——地址几何被「烤」进注册表。为什么地址可以烤进去？因为 cudarc 的设备分配终身不搬家（u2-l4 展开）。
23	
24	一句话定位本讲的文件：`layout.rs` 就是「翻译官」——把 `pegainfer-kv-cache` 的 page-first 几何翻译成 pegaflow 要求的 per-layer strided 注册表。

36	## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解
37	
38	### 4.1 KvArena：一条「等大拷贝单元序列」的抽象
39	
40	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
41	
42	pegaflow 眼里没有「KV cache」，只有**一条条 arena**：从 `base_ptr` 开始，`num_blocks` 个**等大的拷贝单元**，相邻单元起点相距 `block_stride_bytes`。每个拷贝单元 `bytes_per_block` 字节。这就是 `KvArena` 的全部：
43	
44	```rust
45	pub struct KvArena {
46	    name: String,              // 引擎生命周期内save/load 扇出的键
47	    base_ptr: u64,             // arena 起点的裸设备地址
48	    num_blocks: usize,         // 拷贝单元个数（= 池块数）
49	    bytes_per_block: usize,    // 一个拷贝单元的字节数（copy size）
50	    block_stride_bytes: usize, // 相邻单元起点的字节距离（stride）
51	}
52	```
53	
54	（引自 [layout.rs:L21-L27](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-offload/src/layout.rs#L21-L27)，字段注释为讲义所加。）
55	
56	为什么这五个字段就够了？因为「`num_blocks` 个等大单元、固定步长排布」恰好同时刻画了两种真实形态：
57	
58	- **融合布局（qwen3）**：某层的第 `b` 块被其他层的数据隔开，`stride > copy`；
59	- **sidecar / 独立分配（GLM5.2）**：块与块首尾相接，`stride == copy`。
60	
61	抽象的威力在于：pegaflow 完全不需要知道你是什么模型、什么注意力机制，它只会搬「注册在同一个块号下的所有 arena」——文档注释说得很直白：
62	
63	> A fused buffer (qwen3) contributes one arena per model layer; a model with sidecar caches (GLM5.2: MLA latent + index-K per layer, two separate allocations sharing pool block ids) contributes several arenas per model layer — pegaflow moves whatever arenas are registered under one block id together, which is what keeps sidecars in lockstep with their main cache.
64	
65	（[layout.rs:L10-L20](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-offload/src/layout.rs#L10-L20)：这条注释是本讲的纲领——**「注册在同一个块号下的 arena 一起搬」就是 sidecar 与主 KV 保持同步的全部机制**，没有任何额外的锁或协议。）
66	
67	`KvArena` 有三条契约，注意它们**强制方式不同**：
68	
69	| 契约 | 内容 | 强制方式 |
70	|---|---|---|
71	| C1 拷贝不越步长 | `bytes_per_block ≤ block_stride_bytes` | **机器检查**：`from_arenas` 里的 `assert!`（4.3 节） |
72	| C2 名字唯一 | `name` 在引擎生命周期内唯一（save/load 按名字扇出到所有注册层） | **文档契约**：注释要求调用方保证，无断言 |
73	| C3 指针稳定 + 共享块号 | arena 的设备分配终身不搬家；所有 arena 用同一套池块号索引 | **文档契约**：写在 `with_arenas_on` 的文档里（u2-l4 展开） |
74	
75	C2/C3 为什么不做机器检查？因为它们的成立范围（「引擎生命周期」「同一引擎的所有注册」）超出了 `from_arenas` 单次调用的视野——一次调用看不见别的调用。这是 Rust API 设计里很典型的一课：**构造函数只能断言局部不变量，跨调用不变量只能写成文档**。
76	
77	#### 4.1.2 核心流程
78	
79	一个 arena 的逻辑图：
80	
81	```text
82	base_ptr ──► ┌────────┐   ←── block_stride_bytes ──→ ┌────────┐      ┌────────┐
83	             │ block 0│                              │ block 1│ ⋯    │ block N-1│
84	             │ C 字节  │                              │ C 字节  │      │ C 字节   │
85	             └────────┘                              └────────┘      └────────┘
86	             ├──────────── S 字节 ──────────────────────────────────────┤
87	             每块起点：base_ptr + b × S          （b = 0..N-1）
88	             每块拷贝：[base_ptr + b×S, base_ptr + b×S + C)
89	```
90	
91	- 拷第 `b` 块 = 从 `base_ptr + b·S` 读/写连续 `C` 字节；
92	- `S == C`（dense）：块首尾相接，arena 就是一整条连续内存；
93	- `S > C`（strided）：块之间夹着「别人的数据」（融合布局里是其他层），拷贝时必须跳过；
94	- `C > S`：非法——下一个块的开头落在本块数据内部，重叠拷贝，`assert!` 拒绝。

122	#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

136	### 4.2 Registration::from_buffer：把融合缓冲区翻译成 per-layer 视图
137	
138	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
139	
140	先精确刻画 **page-first 融合布局**。`KvBuffer` 是一整块连续显存，按页（块）切分；**每一页内部**按层交错，每层先是 K 再是 V，背靠背：
141	
142	```text
143	┌──────────────────────────── page 0（块 0）────────────────────────────┐
144	│ L0.K │ L0.V │ L1.K │ L1.V │ L2.K │ L2.V │ … │ L7.K │ L7.V           │
145	└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
146	┌──────────────────────────── page 1（块 1）────────────────────────────┐
147	│ L0.K │ L0.V │ L1.K │ L1.V │ …                                        │
148	└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
149	⋮
150	```
151	
152	关键观察有两个，它们分别决定了两个注册参数：
153	
154	1. **页内**，层 ℓ 的 K 紧跟 V，中间没有别人 → 拷贝单元可以是**整个 [K|V] 一段**（`bytes_per_block = layer_bytes`），一段搞定，不需要 K/V 分开。这正是文档里「pegaflow's K/V-split path … does not apply here」的含义——vLLM 的对称布局里 K 和 V 隔开存放，需要两段与 `kv_stride`；我们没有这个问题。
155	2. **跨页**，层 ℓ 的块 `b` 与块 `b+1` 之间隔着**其他所有层**在同页的数据 → 相邻块不连续，`block_stride_bytes = page_stride_bytes`。**stride ≠ copy**，这就是 `block_stride_bytes` 与 `bytes_per_block` 必须解耦的全部动机：拷贝大小（页内一段连续）与块间距（跨页跳一整页）是两个独立的几何量。
156	
157	于是融合布局的翻译规则是：**每个模型层注册成一个 pegaflow 层（一个 arena）**，第 ℓ 个 arena 的 `base_ptr` 整体偏移 ℓ×layer_bytes，stride 用 page_stride，copy 用 layer_bytes。

164	\text{kv\_block\_len} = P \times H \times D
165	\]
166	\[
167	\text{layer\_stride} = 2 \times \text{kv\_block\_len} \qquad (\text{K 接 V})
168	\]
169	\[
170	\text{page\_stride} = L \times \text{layer\_stride} \qquad (\text{页内 } L \text{ 层})
171	\]

173	其中 \(P\) = page_size，\(H\) = num_kv_heads，\(D\) = head_dim，\(L\) = num_layers。

175	层 ℓ 的块 b 的字节地址（本讲的主公式）：

274	### 4.3 Registration::from_arenas：断言、size_bytes 上界与三个单测
275	
276	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
277	
278	`from_arenas` 是两条构造路径的汇合点：`from_buffer`（融合布局自动翻译）和 `with_arenas_on`（调用方自带 arena 列表，sidecar / 共享宿主路径，u2-l4 精读）。它做三件事：
279	
280	1. **执行唯一的机器检查**（C1）：`bytes_per_block ≤ block_stride_bytes`；
281	2. **摊平**：arena 列表 → 八个平行向量；
282	3. **计算 `size_bytes`**：每个 arena 的注册区间长度，采用「最后一块的到达界」公式：
283	
284	\[
285	\text{size\_bytes} = (N_b - 1) \times S + C
286	\]
287	
288	为什么不是直觉的 \(N_b \times S\)?画出来就一目了然：
289	
290	```text
291	base ► ▪────────▪           ▪────────▪           ▪────────▪
292	       │ block0 │  ←gap→    │ block1 │  ←gap→    │ blockN-1│
293	       └────────┘           └────────┘           └────────┘
294	       ├──── (N-1)×S ─────────────────────────────┤← 最后一块的起点
295	       ├──────────────── (N-1)×S + C ─────────────┤← 到达界 = size_bytes
296	       ├──────────────────── N×S ─────────────────┤← 直觉公式：多算了
297	                                                    最后一块后面的 gap
298	```
299	
300	第 \(N_b - 1\) 块的**起点**在 \((N_b-1)\times S\)，拷完它走到 \((N_b-1)\times S + C\)——这就是 arena 真正触碰过的最后一个字节。\(N_b \times S\) 把最后一块**身后那段 gap**也划了进来：那段属于**别人的数据**（融合布局里是同页其他层）。`size_bytes` 是给 pegaflow 做拷贝越界校验用的界（「pegaflow validates copies against this bound」），界本身撒谎会导致：真正的越界拷贝被放过（界太大）、或合法拷贝被误拒（界太小）。所以它必须是**精确的到达界**。
301	
302	另一个统一性细节：`from_arenas` 产出的注册永远是**单段**（`segments = 1`、`kv_stride_bytes = 0`）——因为 arena 的定义就是「一个块一个拷贝单元」，K/V 已在页内连成一段；需要两段与 `kv_stride` 的是 vLLM 的对称布局，那是 vLLM 连接器自己的注册形态，不是本 crate 的。

# u2-l2 GPU 布局映射：从 page-first KvBuffer 到 per-layer strided 注册

## 1. 本讲目标

本讲精读 `pegainfer-kv-offload/src/layout.rs`——整个 crate 里数学密度最高的 100 行。学完后你应该能够：

1. 给定 `(num_layers, kv_heads, head_dim, page_size, num_blocks)`，**手算**出 `kv_block_len / layer_stride / page_stride`（元素数）与 `layer_bytes / page_stride_bytes`（字节数），进而写出每个 layer arena 的 `base_ptr` 偏移、`bytes_per_block`、`block_stride_bytes` 与整个 `Registration` 的 `size_bytes`。
2. 解释 `KvArena` 这个抽象如何用**同一套五个字段**统一两种截然不同的显存形态：qwen3 的融合（fused）布局与 GLM5.2 的 MLA latent + index-K sidecar 布局。
3. 推导 `size_bytes = (num_blocks − 1) × block_stride + bytes_per_block` 为什么是「最后一块的到达界」，而 `num_blocks × stride` 会谎报一段根本不属于本 arena 的尾巴。

本讲不涉及任何 I/O——`layout.rs` 是纯几何，全部逻辑可以在脑子里、纸上跑通。这是它适合作为进阶层第二讲的原因：把地址算对，后面 save/load 的每一步才有意义。

## 2. 前置知识

承接 u1-l2（KV 卸载心智模型）与 u2-l1（配置层）。本讲需要以下几个概念，先用人话过一遍：

- **块（block）与页（page）**：pegainfer 把 KV cache 按 `page_size`（通常 16）个 token 一组切成块。块是搬运单位——save 存的是块，load 恢复的也是块，块的内容寻址键（哈希链）在 u1-l2 讲过。
- **bf16**：brain float 16，2 字节浮点。KV cache 的每个元素是 bf16，所以 `std::mem::size_of::<half::bf16>() == 2`。`pegainfer-kv-cache` 的 `KvLayout` 里所有 stride 都以**元素数**计；要换算成字节必须 ×2。这是本讲最容易算错的一步。
- **stride（步长）与 size（大小）**：一段内存里「相邻两块起点之间的距离」叫 stride，「一块实际占多少字节」叫 copy size / bytes_per_block。GPU 拷贝原语（`cuMemcpyAsync`）只吃**连续区间**；当数据不连续时，就必须告诉底层「每次拷多少、下一块隔多远」——这两个数解耦，正是 `block_stride_bytes` 与 `bytes_per_block` 分开存在的原因。
- **融合（fused）布局**：所有层的 KV 挤在一整块显存分配里，页内按层交错（详见 4.2）。
- **sidecar（边车）布局**：主 KV 之外，每层还有独立分配的辅助状态（GLM5.2 的 index-K），与主 KV **共享同一个块号池**——块号 `b` 同时索引主 KV 的第 `b` 块和 sidecar 的第 `b` 块。
- **注册（registration）**：把 GPU 显存里「哪些区间属于哪些层、块怎么排布」告诉 pegaflow 的一次性动作。注册之后 save/load 都不再传地址，只传 `(层名, 块号)`——地址几何被「烤」进注册表。为什么地址可以烤进去？因为 cudarc 的设备分配终身不搬家（u2-l4 展开）。

一句话定位本讲的文件：`layout.rs` 就是「翻译官」——把 `pegainfer-kv-cache` 的 page-first 几何翻译成 pegaflow 要求的 per-layer strided 注册表。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 | 本讲用到什么 |
|---|---|---|
| `pegainfer-kv-offload/src/layout.rs` | **本讲主角**。`KvArena` 抽象 + `Registration` 两个构造器 + 三个单测 | 全文 |
| `pegainfer-kv-cache/src/layout.rs` | `KvLayout` 纯值类型：page-first 几何的四个维度与三个导出 stride（元素数） | `KvLayout::new` 的三行推导 |
| `pegainfer-kv-cache/src/buffer.rs` | `KvBuffer`：拥有设备内存与几何，不含分配器 | `new`（总元素数）、`device_ptr`（基址稳定性）、`layout()`/`num_blocks()` |
| `pegainfer-kv-offload/src/engine.rs` | `Registration` 的唯一消费者 | `new`/`with_arenas_on` 两条构造路径、`register` 把字段逐个喂给 pegaflow 的批量注册调用 |
| `pegainfer-kv-offload/tests/cpu_roundtrip.rs` | 端到端 roundtrip 集成测试（u1-l3、u3-l4 展开） | 开头的几何常量与「对账断言」——独立复算了一遍本讲的公式 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 KvArena：一条「等大拷贝单元序列」的抽象

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

pegaflow 眼里没有「KV cache」，只有**一条条 arena**：从 `base_ptr` 开始，`num_blocks` 个**等大的拷贝单元**，相邻单元起点相距 `block_stride_bytes`。每个拷贝单元 `bytes_per_block` 字节。这就是 `KvArena` 的全部：

```rust
pub struct KvArena {
    name: String,              // 引擎生命周期内save/load 扇出的键
    base_ptr: u64,             // arena 起点的裸设备地址
    num_blocks: usize,         // 拷贝单元个数（= 池块数）
    bytes_per_block: usize,    // 一个拷贝单元的字节数（copy size）
    block_stride_bytes: usize, // 相邻单元起点的字节距离（stride）
}
```

（引自 [layout.rs:L21-L27](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-offload/src/layout.rs#L21-L27)，字段注释为讲义所加。）

为什么这五个字段就够了？因为「`num_blocks` 个等大单元、固定步长排布」恰好同时刻画了两种真实形态：

- **融合布局（qwen3）**：某层的第 `b` 块被其他层的数据隔开，`stride > copy`；
- **sidecar / 独立分配（GLM5.2）**：块与块首尾相接，`stride == copy`。

抽象的威力在于：pegaflow 完全不需要知道你是什么模型、什么注意力机制，它只会搬「注册在同一个块号下的所有 arena」——文档注释说得很直白：

> A fused buffer (qwen3) contributes one arena per model layer; a model with sidecar caches (GLM5.2: MLA latent + index-K per layer, two separate allocations sharing pool block ids) contributes several arenas per model layer — pegaflow moves whatever arenas are registered under one block id together, which is what keeps sidecars in lockstep with their main cache.

（[layout.rs:L10-L20](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-offload/src/layout.rs#L10-L20)：这条注释是本讲的纲领——**「注册在同一个块号下的 arena 一起搬」就是 sidecar 与主 KV 保持同步的全部机制**，没有任何额外的锁或协议。）

`KvArena` 有三条契约，注意它们**强制方式不同**：

| 契约 | 内容 | 强制方式 |
|---|---|---|
| C1 拷贝不越步长 | `bytes_per_block ≤ block_stride_bytes` | **机器检查**：`from_arenas` 里的 `assert!`（4.3 节） |
| C2 名字唯一 | `name` 在引擎生命周期内唯一（save/load 按名字扇出到所有注册层） | **文档契约**：注释要求调用方保证，无断言 |
| C3 指针稳定 + 共享块号 | arena 的设备分配终身不搬家；所有 arena 用同一套池块号索引 | **文档契约**：写在 `with_arenas_on` 的文档里（u2-l4 展开） |

C2/C3 为什么不做机器检查？因为它们的成立范围（「引擎生命周期」「同一引擎的所有注册」）超出了 `from_arenas` 单次调用的视野——一次调用看不见别的调用。这是 Rust API 设计里很典型的一课：**构造函数只能断言局部不变量，跨调用不变量只能写成文档**。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

一个 arena 的逻辑图：

```text
base_ptr ──► ┌────────┐   ←── block_stride_bytes ──→ ┌────────┐      ┌────────┐
             │ block 0│                              │ block 1│ ⋯    │ block N-1│
             │ C 字节  │                              │ C 字节  │      │ C 字节   │
             └────────┘                              └────────┘      └────────┘
             ├──────────── S 字节 ──────────────────────────────────────┤
             每块起点：base_ptr + b × S          （b = 0..N-1）
             每块拷贝：[base_ptr + b×S, base_ptr + b×S + C)
```

- 拷第 `b` 块 = 从 `base_ptr + b·S` 读/写连续 `C` 字节；
- `S == C`（dense）：块首尾相接，arena 就是一整条连续内存；
- `S > C`（strided）：块之间夹着「别人的数据」（融合布局里是其他层），拷贝时必须跳过；
- `C > S`：非法——下一个块的开头落在本块数据内部，重叠拷贝，`assert!` 拒绝。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

`ELEM_SIZE` 是全文件唯一的常量——元素到字节的换算系数：

- [layout.rs:L7-L8](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-offload/src/layout.rs#L7-L8)：`bf16 KV cache: every layout stride is counted in elements, bytes are ×2.` 定义 `ELEM_SIZE = size_of::<half::bf16>()`。上游 `KvLayout` 的三个 stride 全是元素数，本 crate 边界处统一 ×2 换成字节——**换算只发生在这里一次**，下游（pegaflow 注册、拷贝）全用字节。

### 4.2 Registration::from_buffer：把融合缓冲区翻译成 per-layer 视图

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

先精确刻画 **page-first 融合布局**。`KvBuffer` 是一整块连续显存，按页（块）切分；**每一页内部**按层交错，每层先是 K 再是 V，背靠背：

```text
┌──────────────────────────── page 0（块 0）────────────────────────────┐
│ L0.K │ L0.V │ L1.K │ L1.V │ L2.K │ L2.V │ … │ L7.K │ L7.V           │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌──────────────────────────── page 1（块 1）────────────────────────────┐
│ L0.K │ L0.V │ L1.K │ L1.V │ …                                        │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
⋮
```

关键观察有两个，它们分别决定了两个注册参数：

1. **页内**，层 ℓ 的 K 紧跟 V，中间没有别人 → 拷贝单元可以是**整个 [K|V] 一段**（`bytes_per_block = layer_bytes`），一段搞定，不需要 K/V 分开。这正是文档里「pegaflow's K/V-split path … does not apply here」的含义——vLLM 的对称布局里 K 和 V 隔开存放，需要两段与 `kv_stride`；我们没有这个问题。
2. **跨页**，层 ℓ 的块 `b` 与块 `b+1` 之间隔着**其他所有层**在同页的数据 → 相邻块不连续，`block_stride_bytes = page_stride_bytes`。**stride ≠ copy**，这就是 `block_stride_bytes` 与 `bytes_per_block` 必须解耦的全部动机：拷贝大小（页内一段连续）与块间距（跨页跳一整页）是两个独立的几何量。

于是融合布局的翻译规则是：**每个模型层注册成一个 pegaflow 层（一个 arena）**，第 ℓ 个 arena 的 `base_ptr` 整体偏移 ℓ×layer_bytes，stride 用 page_stride，copy 用 layer_bytes。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

几何推导链（全部源自 `KvLayout::new`，元素数；字节 = 元素数 × 2）：

\[
\text{kv\_block\_len} = P \times H \times D
\]
\[
\text{layer\_stride} = 2 \times \text{kv\_block\_len} \qquad (\text{K 接 V})
\]
\[
\text{page\_stride} = L \times \text{layer\_stride} \qquad (\text{页内 } L \text{ 层})
\]

其中 \(P\) = page_size，\(H\) = num_kv_heads，\(D\) = head_dim，\(L\) = num_layers。

层 ℓ 的块 b 的字节地址（本讲的主公式）：

\[
\text{addr}(b, \ell) = \text{base} + b \times \underbrace{2\,\text{page\_stride}}_{\text{block\_stride\_bytes}} + \ell \times \underbrace{2\,\text{layer\_stride}}_{\text{bytes\_per\_block}}
\]

`from_buffer` 的流程：

```text
输入: &KvBuffer, &CudaStream
 1. layout      = buffer.layout()          # 四个维度 + 三个 stride（元素数）
 2. num_blocks  = buffer.num_blocks()
 3. base_ptr    = buffer.device_ptr(stream) # 融合缓冲区的设备基址
 4. layer_bytes       = layout.layer_stride × 2   # 每层每块的拷贝单元（字节）
    page_stride_bytes = layout.page_stride × 2    # 相邻块间距（字节）
 5. 为每个模型层 ℓ 造一个 arena：
      name = "ℓ", base_ptr = base + ℓ×layer_bytes,
      num_blocks, bytes_per_block = layer_bytes,
      block_stride_bytes = page_stride_bytes
 6. 全部喂给 from_arenas（下一节）
```

```rust
pub(crate) fn from_buffer(buffer: &KvBuffer, stream: &CudaStream) -> Self {
    let layout = buffer.layout();
    let num_blocks = buffer.num_blocks();
    let base_ptr = buffer.device_ptr(stream);

    // One block's copy unit for a layer = its whole [K|V] span in a page.
    let layer_bytes = layout.layer_stride * ELEM_SIZE;
    let page_stride_bytes = layout.page_stride * ELEM_SIZE;

    let arenas: Vec<KvArena> = (0..layout.num_layers)
        .map(|layer| KvArena {
            name: layer.to_string(),
            base_ptr: base_ptr + (layer * layer_bytes) as u64,
            num_blocks,
            bytes_per_block: layer_bytes,
            block_stride_bytes: page_stride_bytes,
        })
        .collect();
    Self::from_arenas(&arenas)
}
```

### 4.3 Registration::from_arenas：断言、size_bytes 上界与三个单测

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

`from_arenas` 是两条构造路径的汇合点：`from_buffer`（融合布局自动翻译）和 `with_arenas_on`（调用方自带 arena 列表，sidecar / 共享宿主路径，u2-l4 精读）。它做三件事：

1. **执行唯一的机器检查**（C1）：`bytes_per_block ≤ block_stride_bytes`；
2. **摊平**：arena 列表 → 八个平行向量；
3. **计算 `size_bytes`**：每个 arena 的注册区间长度，采用「最后一块的到达界」公式：

\[
\text{size\_bytes} = (N_b - 1) \times S + C
\]

为什么不是直觉的 \(N_b \times S\)?画出来就一目了然：

```text
base ► ▪────────▪           ▪────────▪           ▪────────▪
       │ block0 │  ←gap→    │ block1 │  ←gap→    │ blockN-1│
       └────────┘           └────────┘           └────────┘
       ├──── (N-1)×S ─────────────────────────────┤← 最后一块的起点
       ├──────────────── (N-1)×S + C ─────────────┤← 到达界 = size_bytes
       ├──────────────────── N×S ─────────────────┤← 直觉公式：多算了
                                                    最后一块后面的 gap
```

第 \(N_b - 1\) 块的**起点**在 \((N_b-1)\times S\)，拷完它走到 \((N_b-1)\times S + C\)——这就是 arena 真正触碰过的最后一个字节。\(N_b \times S\) 把最后一块**身后那段 gap**也划了进来：那段属于**别人的数据**（融合布局里是同页其他层）。`size_bytes` 是给 pegaflow 做拷贝越界校验用的界（「pegaflow validates copies against this bound」），界本身撒谎会导致：真正的越界拷贝被放过（界太大）、或合法拷贝被误拒（界太小）。所以它必须是**精确的到达界**。

另一个统一性细节：`from_arenas` 产出的注册永远是**单段**（`segments = 1`、`kv_stride_bytes = 0`）——因为 arena 的定义就是「一个块一个拷贝单元」，K/V 已在页内连成一段；需要两段与 `kv_stride` 的是 vLLM 的对称布局，那是 vLLM 连接器自己的注册形态，不是本 crate 的。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```text
输入: &[KvArena]
for arena in arenas:
    assert!(arena.bytes_per_block <= arena.block_stride_bytes)   # C1，违者 panic
    push name / base_ptr
    push size_bytes = (num_blocks - 1) × block_stride_bytes      # 到达界
                      + bytes_per_block
    push num_blocks / bytes_per_block / block_stride_bytes
固定填: kv_stride_bytes = 0, segments = 1     # 单段 arena
输出: Registration（八个平行向量，喂给 register_context_layer_batch_strided）
```

```rust
/// Hand-calc check: NUM_LAYERS=8, NUM_KV_HEADS=4, HEAD_DIM=16,
/// PAGE_SIZE=16, NUM_BLOCKS=64 — the fused-buffer mapping 4.2 derived on paper.
#[test]
fn hand_calc_fused_geometry() {
    const NUM_LAYERS: usize = 8;
    const NUM_KV_HEADS: usize = 4;
    const HEAD_DIM: usize = 16;
    const PAGE_SIZE: usize = 16;
    const NUM_BLOCKS: usize = 64;

    // KvLayout::new 的三条公式（元素数），再 ×ELEM_SIZE 换字节。
    let kv_block_len = PAGE_SIZE * NUM_KV_HEADS * HEAD_DIM; // 1024
    let layer_stride = 2 * kv_block_len;                    // 2048
    let page_stride = NUM_LAYERS * layer_stride;            // 16384
    let layer_bytes = layer_stride * ELEM_SIZE;             // 4096
    let page_stride_bytes = page_stride * ELEM_SIZE;        // 32768

    let arenas: Vec<KvArena> = (0..NUM_LAYERS)

            name: l.to_string(),
            base_ptr: (l * layer_bytes) as u64,
            num_blocks: NUM_BLOCKS,
            bytes_per_block: layer_bytes,
            block_stride_bytes: page_stride_bytes,
        })
        .collect();

    assert_eq!(reg.layer_names, ["0","1","2","3","4","5","6","7"]);
    assert_eq!(reg.bytes_per_block, vec![4096; NUM_LAYERS]);
    assert_eq!(reg.block_stride_bytes, vec![32768; NUM_LAYERS]);
    assert_eq!(reg.num_blocks, vec![NUM_BLOCKS; NUM_LAYERS]);
    assert_eq!(reg.segments, vec![1; NUM_LAYERS]);        // 单段 arena
    assert_eq!(reg.kv_stride_bytes, vec![0; NUM_LAYERS]);
    assert_eq!(reg.data_ptrs[7], 7 * 4096);               // 逐层偏移 ℓ×layer_bytes
    // 到达界：63×32768 + 4096 = 2_068_480，且与手算 2_068_480 逐字相等
    assert_eq!(reg.size_bytes, vec![63 * 32768 + 4096; NUM_LAYERS]);
    assert_eq!(reg.size_bytes[0], 2_068_480);
```

**练习 2**：`interleaved_arena_size_is_last_block_reach` 里 `num_blocks=4, copy=512, stride=4096`。验证 12 800，并算 `4 × 4096` 会是多少。

**答案**：\((4-1)\times 4\,096 + 512 = 12\,288 + 512 = 12\,800\)；直觉公式给 \(16\,384\)，多出的 3 584 = 4 096 − 512 又是 `stride − copy`。

**练习 3**：`arena_copy_unit_must_fit_its_stride` 为什么把 `num_blocks` 设成 1 就够了？

- **`KvArena` 五字段**（name / base_ptr / num_blocks / bytes_per_block / block_stride_bytes）把「等大拷贝单元 + 固定步长」抽象出来，一套字段同时表达 qwen3 的融合布局（stride > copy）与 GLM5.2 的 sidecar 布局（stride == copy、逐层多个 arena 共享块号）。
- **融合布局翻译规则**（`from_buffer`）：每模型层一个 arena，`base_ptr = base + ℓ×layer_bytes`、`bytes_per_block = layer_bytes`（页内 K|V 连续，单段拷贝）、`block_stride_bytes = page_stride_bytes`（跨块被同页其他层隔开）——stride 与 copy size 解耦是这套布局能注册进 pegaflow 的关键。

- **可见性即设计**：`KvArena` 未从 lib.rs 导出、字段私有，对账测试因此必须住在 `src/layout.rs` 内部——测试的位置本身就是 API 边界的注脚。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

- **下一讲 u2-l4（引擎构造与注册）**：看 `Registration` 的完整消费链——`OffloadEngine::new`（走 `from_buffer`）与 `with_arenas_on`（走 `from_arenas`，sidecar / DP-rank 共享宿主的真实入口）如何把本讲的八个向量喂给 `register_context_layer_batch_strided`，以及 `page_first` 标志何时翻转。也可先读 u2-l3（共享宿主 OffloadHost）补齐 host 侧背景。
- **源码延伸**：`pegainfer-kv-cache/src/buffer.rs` 的 `copy_page`（整页 D2D 拷贝）用的是同一套 page-first 几何，可作交叉印证；`engine.rs` 里 `register` 之后的 `layer_names` 保存（save/load 扇出的键）承接本讲的 name 契约。
- **高级方向（u3-l4）**：逐行解剖 `tests/cpu_roundtrip.rs`，看几何常量如何在端到端 GPU→CPU→GPU 字节级回归里扮演「期望值生成器」——本讲的手算正是那个测试的地基。

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. - IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
